A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiOpt by the same authors despite the changed title. All 13 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 Tables 1–4 report original experiments on synthetic optimization, wireless power allocation, ACOPF, and motion retargeting.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, a two-dimensional diagnostic experiment, training trajectories, and extensive appendix sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: V1 Algorithm 1 bootstraps without solution labels from the outset. V2 Algorithm 1 first trains on optimal solutions for a supervised fraction of training, defaulting to 0.2, before bootstrapping. This introduces a substantial training phase; weighting, resetting, the memory buffer, equality completion, and solution selection largely persist.

E1.justification: V2 adds a convex-QP benchmark and a two-dimensional QP diagnostic, removes wireless power allocation, and adds a squared-norm constraint to retargeting in Appendix E.5. Both ACOPF57 and ACOPF118 were already specified in v1 Appendix A.2.3; their separate reporting does not constitute newly added coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator families largely persist. V2's MLP uses equality completion, whereas v1's direct-prediction NN reports nonzero equality residuals. Separate diffusion-without-selection benchmark rows disappear, although K=1 remains in sampling analyses. Both MBD completion variants remain in v2 Table 3.

E3.justification: V2 adds optimality-gap and feasibility-rate metrics and controlled hyperparameter sweeps. Reported settings change substantially: QPSR's alpha changes from 10 to 1, MBD samples increase from 100 to 256, hidden width increases from 256 to 512, and retargeting examples decrease from 1,836 to 1,737. Diffusion sampling budgets also change.

E4.justification: V1 mainly examines solution selection and MBD completion through benchmark comparisons. V2 adds distribution visualizations, training trajectories, and Appendix D studies of diffusion steps, supervision fraction, training samples, inference samples, and noise level, including runtime–feasibility trade-offs.

E5.justification: V1 Section 5.1 explicitly specifies five repetitions per baseline and task for means and standard deviations. V2 retains mean-and-standard-deviation reporting but omits the repetition count. This removes statistical-procedure documentation without establishing that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Benchmark values are extensively replaced: DiOpt's QPSR objective changes from -111.619 in v1 Table 2 to -9.53 in v2 Table 1 under revised objective and training settings. V2 adds convex-QP results, separate ACOPF118 rows, gap and feasibility entries, and numerous diagnostic findings. These do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 introduces Theorem 1 and Appendix A's claimed approximately 2^-d local feasibility probability for LPs with random constraint normals. Appendix B adds a concentration derivation motivating resetting. V1 contains no corresponding theorem or proofs. The new LP proof does not clearly justify transferring its region-symmetry argument to the selected optimum.

C1.justification: V1 presents a fully self-supervised solver and claims the first successful integration of self-supervised diffusion with hard constraints. V2 reframes the contributions around analyzing supervised diffusion's infeasibility and developing a supervised-plus-self-supervised framework. The new theoretical contribution and dependence on labeled solutions materially redefine the central claims.

C2.justification: V2 recasts the buffer as protection against sampling regressions and explains why limited supervision can harm objective quality. Appendix D adds interpretations of noise-driven exploration and acknowledges that sampling farther inside the feasible region can hurt retargeting performance. V1's training-efficiency and equality-completion limitations remain in abbreviated form.

D1.justification: V2 Appendices C/F substantially expand architecture, time-embedding, training-schedule, hardware, and baseline-pseudocode details. Conversely, v1's batch size, learning rate, and DC3 implementation-source URL disappear. Sampling-setting descriptions in Appendices C and D.4 conflict over the main comparisons, limiting reproducibility despite the expanded documentation.

R1.justification: Most of the three-part related-work survey remains. V2 adds positioning against gauge flow matching and explicitly distinguishes continuous optimization from unsupervised combinatorial diffusion, citing additional work by Karalias–Loukas and Sanokowski et al. Geometric-probability and DDIM/SDE references are added, while several application-specific references are removed.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its abstract and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten, and task-by-task experimental exposition becomes benchmarking and training-dynamics sections. A separate analysis section precedes methodology, and the appendices are reorganized into proofs, settings, ablations, benchmark definitions, and baseline descriptions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Retained conceptual and workflow diagrams are relocated, while new scatterplots and extensive training/sensitivity panels are added. Results are reorganized into cross-task tables with gap/feasibility columns and check/cross markers; the previous hyperparameter grid is replaced by a symbol table and prose.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mostly endpoint benchmarks, v2's toy example and Appendix D substantially improve empirical diagnosis. However, the new LP proof leaves its transfer from region symmetry to the selected optimum unjustified, ACOPF57 feasibility differs between Tables 1 and 3 (87.00% versus 79.11%) without explanation, and run-count and training details are lost. These gains and unresolved validity/reproducibility problems prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
